issues.description: The template and the solution use different getter method names for StockIngredient, which creates a structural inconsistency: the template's StockIngredient exposes getIngredientName() while the solution's StockIngredient exposes getName(). Corresponding usages in Stock.findStockIngredient also differ (template calls getIngredientName(), solution calls getName()). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not standardize the exact method names. This mismatch can confuse students comparing template and solution code and may cause tests or example code that expect one name to fail against the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose and document a single, consistent getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across all artifacts (either getName() or getIngredientName()). Update the template StockIngredient and Stock.findStockIngredient to use that name, align the solution accordingly, and add a precise note in the problem statement instructing students which getter names to implement so all code and tests remain consistent.

issues.description: The StockIngredient 'name' accessor is named getIngredientName() in the template code but getName() in the solution. The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" and the UML uses the field name 'name', but does not specify an accessor name. This cross-artifact difference (template vs solution) can create unnecessary confusion about which getter students should implement and which name their code should call (e.g., in Stock.findStockIngredient).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the accessor name for the StockIngredient.name field across template and solution. Preferred fix: rename the template's getIngredientName() to getName() and update all references (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to call getName(). Alternatively, change the solution to use getIngredientName() consistently. Also add a short note in the problem statement about the expected getter naming convention to avoid ambiguity.
